weeks.week_title: Week 1: Why the Order Was Founded / Mission and Historical Need

required_reading.title: Corporal School — 8 Week Lesson Plan Program

memory_targets: The First Crusade took place from 1095 to 1099.
Pilgrims traveling to Jerusalem faced serious danger.
The earliest Templar mission centered on protection and religious purpose.

weeks.week_title: Week 2: Founders, Early Support, and Legitimacy

required_reading.title: Corporal School — 8 Week Lesson Plan Program

memory_targets: Hugh de Payns is the founder most closely linked to the order.
Baldwin II granted the Templars quarters near the Temple Mount.
Formal recognition at Troyes and later privileges increased legitimacy and growth.

weeks.week_title: Week 3: Growth, Expansion, and Public Trust

required_reading.title: Corporal School — 8 Week Lesson Plan Program

memory_targets: The Templars gained support through service, discipline, and reliability.
Roads, strongholds, and logistics helped support pilgrim protection and wider operations.
Growth required integrity, not merely efficiency.

weeks.week_title: Week 4: Structure, Offices, and Daily Life

required_reading.title: Corporal School — 8 Week Lesson Plan Program

memory_targets: The order included knights, sergeants, and chaplains.
The Grand Master, Seneschal, Marshal, and Preceptor held important leadership roles.
Templar life combined prayer, obedience, discipline, and service.

weeks.week_title: Week 5: Spiritual Discipline, Service, and the Corporal Rank

required_reading.title: Corporal School — 8 Week Lesson Plan Program

memory_targets: A Corporal must remain current with classwork and attend meetings, Bible studies, and Round Tables.
Ranks exist for service and responsibility, not self-exaltation.
Christian knighthood requires integrity, humility, and faithful participation.

weeks.week_title: Week 6: Wealth, Power, Risks, and Mission Drift

required_reading.title: Corporal School — 8 Week Lesson Plan Program

memory_targets: The Templars became important as logisticians, administrators, and financial custodians.
Wealth and reputation increased both influence and danger.
The fall of Acre in 1291 weakened the order’s original military purpose.

weeks.week_title: Week 7: Crisis, Friday the 13th, and Suppression

required_reading.title: Corporal School — 8 Week Lesson Plan Program
HISTORY: Friday the 13th and the Knights Templar

memory_targets: The arrests in France took place on Friday, October 13, 1307.
Pope Clement V suppressed the order in 1312 under strong pressure.
The charges and confessions must be taught with attention to coercion and political context.

weeks.week_title: Week 8: Jacques de Molay, Fall of the Order, Historical Importance

required_reading.title: Corporal School — 8 Week Lesson Plan Program
National Geographic: Friday the 13th and Templar Myth
HISTORY: Friday the 13th and the Knights Templar

memory_targets: Jacques de Molay is remembered as the last grand master of the order.
Friday, October 13, 1307 is a real historical date in the Templar story.
The later superstition of Friday the 13th should be taught cautiously, not as certain origin fact.
